Consistent qualitative pattern: fading extreme funding is weakly positive and following it is reliably negative (A2 t=-2.0, A4 t=-2.1, E2 t=-5.0), i.e. the perp premium does NOT continue, but the fade is too small (gross ~6-11 $/contract per 8h on $3-6k notional, ~0.1-0.2%) to clear MBT costs with significance. Funding extremes are regime-clustered (abs thresholds fire almost only in 2020-21 and 2024H1; in 2022-23 the rate is pinned at 0.01%), so any absolute-threshold rule has essentially one or two years of data. ETH/MET is structurally uneconomic at this cost: $0.92 RT on 0.1 ETH (~$200-400 notional) is 0.25-0.45% of notional per round turn, so even 8h holds have avg wins of ~$4; every ETH variant is negative net. DATA/ALIGNMENT: 5-min bars; funding settled at T is attached to the bar with open_time==T and acted on at the open of T+5m (conservative; the rate is visible as Binance's predicted rate before T); rolling z/percentile windows use only settlements strictly before T; the pre-settlement variant uses the rate settled at T-8h. Hold 'to next funding' = 94 bars (7h50m) so the next settlement signal is not blocked by the open position. The one-trade-at-a-time engine, Topstep hours, 15:10 CT flat and $3.82/$0.92 costs are applied. IMPORTANT PROTOCOL BUG FOUND: protocol.forced_flat_time() returns True for every bar with CT time >= 15:10 (the whole 15:10-24:00 CT span), not just the 15:10-17:00 break. In protocol.backtest_signals any position entered in the evening session (17:00-24:00 CT, allowed by entry_mask and by the documented rules) is closed on its own entry bar at the entry price for a pure cost loss (hold_bars=0). For this family the 00:00 UTC settlement (18:00/19:00 CT) is affected: e.g. 114 of A1's 355 trades were zero-duration -$3.82 losers under the as-is engine. The script therefore uses backtest_signals_fixed (verbatim copy with the flat condition reduced to `not tradable_mask`, which already forces the exit at the open of the 15:10 CT bar and before the weekend); the as-is protocol numbers are stored per variant in /home/user/j/results/research/funding_signal.json under protocol_asis (t-stats are listed in each variant's by_year string as protocol_asis_t). This bug will affect every family that enters after 17:00 CT and any verifier that uses protocol.backtest_signals unchanged; the fix is a one-line change in protocol.forced_flat_time (restrict to 15:10<=t<17:00 CT) or dropping the flat_now term in backtest_signals. Side note for whoever uses these as CME proxies: funding-settlement effects (M1/M2) are perp-specific order flow and would transmit to CME micro futures only partially; they showed no edge even in the perp itself. Full per-variant stats (bootstrap CI, drawdown, exit reasons, L/S split, n_signals) are in the JSON; runtime ~9 s.

Every variant has mean_net < 0; the best are BTC_60m_z3_rev_h60_down_only (gross +$0.92/contract, net -$2.90, t=-1.7) and BTC_30m_z3_cont_h60_oi_build (gross +$1.81, net -$2.01, t=-0.9); none passes any part of the screen. Full stats incl. bootstrap CI, exit reasons and deflated Sharpe are in /home/user/j/research/hyp/vol_regime_reversal_results.json. Signal construction: realised vol from the 24h (288-bar) window ending BEFORE the move (shift k), fresh-crossing events only (one shock = one trade), OI aligned with merge_asof on snapshot time <= bar open (>=5 min stale at decision), thresholds (z 3/4, volume-ratio 4, dOI -0.5%/+0.3%) fixed from feature quantiles before any P&L was computed. No-cost diagnostics (all events, no hours filter) explain the failure: the symmetric mean reversal after a 3-sigma move is only +1 to +7 bp over the next 30-240 min (t <= 2.3), far below the round-trip cost expressed in notional (MBT $3.82 = ~6-13 bp of 0.1 BTC; MET $0.92 = ~25-50 bp of 0.1 ETH, which makes MET intraday scalping essentially unviable: ETH win rates 24-29% with avg win ~= avg loss ~= $2). The only consistent raw effect is directional: DOWN moves partially revert (BTC k=12 H=60min +11 bp t=+2.6; ETH k=12 +17 bp t=+3.2) while UP moves continue (ETH k=6 follow-up +10 bp t=-2.9 for the fade), consistent with long-liquidation cascades in thin books; but splitting by Topstep tradability shows the reversal is concentrated OFF Topstep hours (weekends / 15:10-17:00 CT break): BTC 30-min down moves +19 bp t=+3.7 off-hours vs +0.2 bp t=+0.1 in-hours; 60-min +23 bp t=+3.6 vs +7 bp t=+1.3; ETH similar (+24 bp vs +4 bp). I.e. the liquidation-wick reversal exists mainly in thin weekend/overnight books that a Topstep MBT/MET trader is not allowed to hold through, and in-hours the residual is below costs. Volume conditioning (ratio >= 4) and OI-drop conditioning did not isolate a tradable subset (OI-drop fades are the worst BTC variant, -$7.78/trade); the OI-build continuation sign is right but weak. A 1% stop made the fade worse (649/1938 stopped). Not recommended for further in-sample tuning; a possible future (different) family is exchange-specific liquidation data rather than price-z-scores, but it would still be subject to the weekend exclusion.

RESULT: nothing found. 0 of 18 variants (13 pre-specified + 5 post-hoc) pass the screen (n>=150, mean_net>0, t>=2.5, >=3 positive years). Results JSON with full stats, exit-reason counts, by-side means and diagnostics: /home/user/j/research/hyp/vwap_reversion_results.json.

BASE rule (shared by every variant; the per-variant 'rule' lists the deviations): 5-min bars from Binance USDT-M perp as the MBT/MET proxy. Session = calendar day anchored at 00:00 UTC (or 17:00 CT where stated). tp=(high+low+close)/3; vwap = cumulative sum(volume*tp)/sum(volume) within the session; sd = sqrt(sum(volume*tp^2)/sum(volume) - vwap^2) (volume-weighted st.dev. of tp around VWAP, the classic VWAP-sd band); z=(close-vwap)/sd. Signal at the close of bar i when |z[i]|>=K and |z[i-1]|<K (fresh crossing, one trade per excursion), at least 12 bars into the session, and |close-vwap| >= 3 x round-trip cost / 0.1 ($114.6 MBT, $27.6 MET; the distance must be worth 3 round trips). Enter at the open of bar i+1 with side=-sign(z) (fade). Exit at the open of bar j+1 when at the close of bar j |z[j]|<=0.2 or z changed sign (back at VWAP), or |z[j]|>=K+1.5 (soft stop), or bar j is the last bar of the session (VWAP resets); otherwise at the open of the bar 48 bars (4h) after entry, or at the 15:10 CT Topstep flat. No fixed stop/target. One position at a time, Topstep hours via protocol.backtest_signals. All thresholds fixed before any P&L was computed.

WHY IT FAILS (diagnostics, no costs, no hours filter, measured from the open of bar i+1): after a fresh 2.5-sd excursion from the UTC-day VWAP, BTC moves back toward VWAP by only +4.7/+4.5/+6.0/+9.6 bp over 30/60/120/240 min (median distance to VWAP 120 bp, i.e. ~0% of the distance is recovered on average); ETH +6.8/+4.6/+5.3/+7.4 bp on a 156 bp distance. Fresh 2.0-sd excursions: +2 bp. 3.0-sd excursions with the 17:00 CT anchor recover the most (+30 bp / 19% at 2h, +43 bp / 27% at 4h, t~3) but on only ~355 events and it does not survive costs or the year split. MBT round-trip cost is 6-38 bp of notional depending on BTC price level (38 bp at $10k in 2020, 13 bp at $30k, 6 bp at $65k), MET 46 bp at $2000 ETH and >100 bp in 2020. Gross P&L of the base BTC variant is already negative (-$2.14/trade): trades that reach VWAP earn +$21.6 net on average (472 of 931), but the 4h time exits lose -$41.1 (334) and the forced flats -$16.2 (125); the classic negative skew of fading, with no positive drift to pay for it.

THE FAMILY'S CONDITIONING IS BACKWARDS IN-SAMPLE: conditional on the trailing-24h realised vol being BELOW its 30-day median, 2.5-sd excursions CONTINUE (BTC -9.6 bp toward VWAP at 2h, t -3.3; rv<=0.7: -11.7 bp, t -2.5; ETH -11.1 bp, t -3.6), i.e. a 2.5-sd move off a narrow quiet-day band is a breakout, not a stretched rubber band. Reversion exists only in HIGH-vol regimes (rv ratio >1: BTC +23.9 bp t +4.3, ETH +23.6 bp t +2.9) and only after DOWN excursions (BTC +18.5 bp t +3.7; up excursions -5.2 bp), which is the liquidation-wick effect already catalogued by the vol_regime_reversal family rather than a VWAP effect. The low-vol-filtered variants are accordingly the worst (BTC lowvol -$12.94/trade, t -4.8). The choppy-session (efficiency ratio<=0.3) filter removes almost nothing (97% of signals pass) and does not help. The post-hoc high-vol/long-only variants that trade the diagnostic directly are flat after costs (t 0.66 at best) and sign-flip by year (positive 2020-21, negative 2022-24), so they are not nominated.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES: (1) The soft stop at |z|>=K+1.5 never fires because a VWAP-sd band inflates with the excursion itself (99.9th pct of |z| = 3.0); the nostop variant is therefore identical to the base and is counted but uninformative. (2) protocol.forced_flat_time flags every bar with CT time >= 15:10 including the 17:00-24:00 CT evening session, which would close every evening entry on its own entry bar; as in the sibling families it was patched for the duration of each backtest to flag only the 15:10-17:00 CT break (daytime behaviour identical: exit at the open of the 15:10 CT bar). (3) No funding or metrics data used; no look-ahead: all features at bar i use bars <= i and the engine acts at the open of bar i+1; the rv reference median ends at bar i-1. (4) Runtime ~5 s for all 18 variants plus diagnostics. Deflated-Sharpe inputs: n_variants = 18 for this family.

# Synthesis: 0 of 196 in-sample variants survived; nothing reached the holdout

## Bottom line

- **No in-sample survivor was nominated** by any of the 12 hypothesis families (196 logged variants: session_drift 21, funding_signal 20, positioning_metrics 19, vwap_reversion 18, volume_time_seasonality 16, intraday_momentum 15, vol_regime_reversal 15, calendar_events 15, range_breakout 15, weekend_monday 15, cross_asset_leadlag 14, taker_imbalance 13).
- The survivor bar was mean_net > 0, t >= 2.5, n >= 150, net > 0 in >= 3 calendar years. Nothing met it. `SURVIVORS = []`, `VERDICTS = []`, `/home/user/j/research/verify/` is empty, and the holdout (2024-07-01 .. 2026-10-31, `data_research/HO`) was never opened.
- **Nothing survives both holdout replication and audit, because nothing was tested on the holdout.** The ranked list is therefore empty, and there is nothing to price through the Topstep dynamic program.

## Why "nothing" is the correct reading, not a near miss

The max in-sample net t-stat with n >= 150 was **+2.07** (range_breakout, post-hoc wide-range ORB filter). Across ~196 trials (roughly 120-140 effectively independent, since long/short mirrors are exact negatives minus 2x cost), the expected maximum of pure-noise t-stats is about sqrt(2 ln N) ~ 3.1-3.25. The observed best is *below* the noise ceiling, which is what a search over zero-edge signals with a fixed cost drag looks like. The strongly negative t-stats in taker_imbalance (-6.96) and cross_asset_leadlag (-6.39) are cost drag on ~zero gross, not sign-flippable signals.

The structural reason, consistent across every family: round-turn cost vs. gross edge.
- MBT: $3.82 RT = 6-38 bp of a 0.1-BTC notional depending on price level (38 bp at $10k in 2020, ~13 bp at $30k, ~6 bp at $65k).
- MET: $0.92 RT = 25-100+ bp of a 0.1-ETH notional. **Every ETH variant in every family was net negative**; MET is structurally uneconomic for any hold shorter than many hours at in-sample prices.
- Every gross intraday effect found was 1-10 bp. Regression-level relations do exist (below) but are an order of magnitude too small for one micro contract.

## Nearest misses (for the record; NOT to be promoted to holdout)

| Family | Variant | Sym | n | trades/day | mean net $/contract | t | win rate | avg win / loss | Why it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| range_breakout | BTC_us_orb30_wide_rangestop_flat | BTC | 659 | 0.56 | +5.58 | 2.07 | 0.426 | 60.6 / 35.4 | post-hoc (mirror of a losing narrow filter), 2020 = -$740, DSR 0.62 at 15 trials |
| funding_signal | A14_tail_short_abs1e-3_4h | BTC | 63 | 0.054 | +26.8 | 2.57 | 0.619 | 70.3 / 43.9 | n=63; 100% of P&L in 2021, zero signals 2022-24 |
| positioning_metrics | O4_oi_build_follow_4h_h4 | BTC | 201 | 0.31 | +6.57 | 1.65 | 0.507 | 46.6 / 34.7 | only 3 years of OI data; relaxed (O9) and ETH twin (E4, t -1.72) do not confirm; DSR p 0.41 |
| funding_signal | A5_fade_pct95_8h | BTC | 307 | 0.26 | +7.49 | 1.56 | 0.505 | 62.5 / 48.6 | 2021-dominated, DSR p 0.37 |
| calendar_events | BTC_mexp_lasthour_fade_4h | BTC | 54 | 0.046 | +18.9 | 1.37 | 0.667 | 52.5 / 48.3 | n=54 |
| weekend_monday | BTC_gapfollow_1pct | BTC | 126 | 0.11 | +16.1 | 1.20 | 0.444 | 133.7 / 77.9 | n=126, 2020 negative; plain gap-follow (session_drift) only t 1.08 |

If the orchestrator insists on running the Topstep DP on any of these as a sensitivity exercise, these are the inputs (`--win_rate --avg_win --avg_loss --trades_per_day --n`), but the output would be an in-sample, post-selection upper bound, not a forecast. The evaluator smoke test (`results/research/evaluator_smoke.log`) already shows how fragile the DP is: a hypothetical p_win 0.54 edge at 2 trades/day prices at P_pass 1.00, but at p_win -2se (0.49) the EV is -inf. A few hundred holdout trades cannot pin a win rate to +/-2%, so even a genuine survivor would carry a wide EV band; an unverified near-miss priced this way is worthless.

**Recommendation: do not open the holdout for these.** Spending the sealed window on nearest-misses selected from 196 trials would both contaminate it for a future cycle and produce a holdout t >= 1.5 by chance with high probability.

## Robust diagnostic-level relations (regression-level only, post hoc, all below micro costs)

These are the only things in the whole search that look like real structure. They are not tradable at MBT/MET costs as 1-hour rules and must be re-specified as a pre-registered family on in-sample before any holdout exposure:

1. **Day-so-far -> last UTC hour continuation**: regression t +7.55 (BTC) / +7.51 (ETH), ~+9 bp conditional. Traded as a 1-hour rule it nets +$0.15 (t 0.19).
2. **Overnight (17:00 CT -> 08:30 CT) -> US session reversal**: t -4.40 / -4.03. Fade version +$3.90, t 0.75, 2021-driven.
3. **US-session ORB continuation**: raw +8 bp at 1h (t 2.8), +17 bp at 4h (t 3.3), +25 bp at 12h (t 3.0) on 1021 events; traded versions t 0.5-2.1.
4. **3-sigma down-move reversal** exists (+11 to +23 bp) but is concentrated off Topstep hours (weekends / 15:10-17:00 CT break); in-hours residual is +0.2 to +7 bp.
5. **Rising OI confirms trend** (O4 +, its fade mirror O5 t -2.63); **fading extreme funding** weakly positive, following it reliably negative.
6. **16:00-17:00 CT** is the strongest positive hour for both symbols (t 3.4 / 3.2) and sits inside the CME daily break where no position may be held.

Any future family built on these should amortise the fixed cost (multi-hour to full-session holds, large conditional moves, BTC only), and should count the 196 prior trials in its deflation to the extent it reuses the same data and signals.

## Protocol defect that must be fixed before any holdout verifier runs

Confirmed by reading `/home/user/j/research/protocol.py:57-61`: `forced_flat_time()` returns `minutes >= 15*60+10` with no upper bound, so it flags the entire 15:10-24:00 CT span, and `backtest_signals` (line 145, `flat_now`) closes every evening-session (17:00-24:00 CT) entry on its own entry bar for a pure -cost loss. This contradicts the docstring and the Topstep rules in the module header. All 12 families worked around it with local monkeypatches or copied engines (`forced_flat_break_only`, `backtest_signals_fixed`, `run_engine`, `backtest_levels`), which means the canonical engine and the per-family engines currently disagree. Fix: restrict to `(minutes >= 910) & (minutes < 1020)` (weekend flatness is already enforced by `tradable_mask`). Until this is applied in `protocol.py`, a verifier that uses the unpatched engine on any evening/Sunday-entry rule will produce meaningless numbers.

## Data limits worth carrying forward

- OI / long-short metrics only from 2022-01; top-trader ratios only from 2023-01, so positioning families had 2-3 calendar years, not 4.5.
- Holdout prices (BTC well above in-sample levels for most of 2024-07 onward) make the MBT cost a smaller fraction of notional (~<= 6 bp above $60k), so the cost-in-bp regime of the holdout is friendlier than 2020-22 in-sample. This is a reason to design the next in-sample cycle around BTC-only, longer-hold rules, not a reason to test the current near-misses on the holdout.

## What the next step should do

1. Treat the Topstep pricing step as having **no input**: the expected edge for this program, on these signal classes at micro-contract costs, is zero.
2. Apply the one-line `forced_flat_time` fix in `protocol.py` and re-run one family as a regression check so canonical and patched engines agree.
3. Keep the holdout sealed. If another research cycle is run, pre-register a small number of cost-amortising BTC families derived from relations 1-3 above, with the 196 prior variants counted in the deflation.
